summary:
Lunar Site Navigator is an interactive platform designed to evaluate potential landing sites near the Moon's South Pole. The project combines NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris data, an interactive 3D lunar globe, a polar sky-dome tracker, and terrain-masked 24-hour sunlight analysis to help users understand the environmental conditions of different lunar locations.

The platform aims to support future lunar exploration by providing insights into sunlight availability, terrain conditions, and landing site suitability. By bringing complex lunar data into an accessible visual interface, Lunar Site Navigator helps researchers, students, and space enthusiasts explore potential landing locations and better understand the challenges of lunar missions.
details:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a web-based project designed to help users explore potential lunar landing locations through interactive visualizations.

The platform provides a 3D Moon visualization, mission parameters, Earth-Moon visualization, and lunar exploration information. It aims to make lunar landing site exploration easier to understand and more engaging.

The project focuses on presenting lunar exploration concepts through an interactive and user-friendly website. Users can explore the Moon and understand different aspects of lunar missions.

The website was developed using Google AI Studio with web development technologies. Our goal is to support space exploration education and inspire interest in future lunar missions.
